analysis: The change is confined to scripts/test-provider-release-toolchain.py, a test-only file. It adds a read_github_env helper and new unit tests for scripts/prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh. The tests cover SDK 27.0/27.2 acceptance in qualification mode, release mode accepting only SDK 27.2 with Swift 6.4.2, refusal of an unknown DARKBLOOM_PROVIDER_TOOLCHAIN value, and refusal of wrong, malformed or missing SDK versions and of old or unparsable Swift. They also cover preference for the 27.2 directory in the CLT layout, and Xcode selection through stubbed xcrun, xcode-select and xcodebuild. The tests use temp directories and stub binaries only. They make no network calls, no secret handling, and no changes to runtime provider, coordinator, attestation or cache code, so no threat-model assets or boundaries (TB-002, TB-003, TB-007, TB-011, T-041) are affected at runtime. The tests tighten supply-chain posture by asserting that release builds fail closed without SDK 27.2 / Swift 6.4.2 and that an explicit DEVELOPER_DIR is the only candidate. They cannot show that the unseen shell script actually implements this behavior; that script's diff was not in this batch, so the tests' claims about it are unverified. The security-relevant integration question is whether prepare-provider-release-toolchain.sh changes in the PR match the asserted behavior, specifically the version regex that rejects 6.4.20 and the release-mode gating. No findings.
